```{r setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
coding_all <- read.csv("coding.csv")
sample_info <- read.csv("sample.csv")
screen <- read.csv("screen.csv")
## genomics-only papers are excluded from the denominator (coding_rules.md)
genomics_only <- grepl("^genomics", coding_all$model_class)
coding <- coding_all[!genomics_only, ]
glm <- filter(coding, uses_glm_2plus == "y")
n_emp <- nrow(coding)
n_glm <- nrow(glm)
## count, percentage and exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% CI
pct <- function(x, n) {
  ci <- 100 * binom.test(x, n)$conf.int
  sprintf("%d/%d (%.0f%%; %.0f–%.0f%%)", x, n, 100 * x / n, ci[1], ci[2])
}
```

## Background

@forstmeierCryptic2011 surveyed the September 2007 issues of
*The American Naturalist*, *Animal Behaviour*, *Ecology*, *Evolution* and
*Proceedings of the Royal Society B*:

> 28 out of 50 empirical studies (56%) use GLMs with two or more explanatory
> variables. Of these, six studies fitted between 6 and 17 predictors, three
> of them with N/k < 3. Interactions were considered in 80% of the studies,
> and six of 11 experimental studies included treatment-by-covariate
> interactions. All 16 models with more than five predictors (including
> interactions) were simplified (15 by backward elimination, one by forward
> selection), and only 2 of 28 studies presented the full model.

## Methods

- **Sampling frame:** all research articles in the September 2026 print
  issues (Am Nat 208(3), Anim Behav, Ecology 107(9), Evolution 80(9)) and the
  September 2026 issues of Proc B (293(2078–2079)); `r nrow(screen)` articles.
- **Screening:** titles and abstracts were used to classify each article as
  empirical or not (reviews, theory/simulation, methods, comments);
  `r sum(screen$empirical == "y")` were empirical.
- **Sample:** 10 empirical papers per journal were drawn at random (seed
  20261112), or all of them when a journal had fewer than 10 (Am Nat: 5).
- **Coding:** each paper's methods and results were coded for the fields in
  F&S's paragraph. The coding rules are in `coding_rules.md`. The main
  differences from a literal reading of "GLM" are:
  - mixed models count;
  - GAMs and Bayesian regressions do not count;
  - genomics analyses (e.g. per-gene differential expression) do not count,
    and papers whose only analyses are genomic are dropped from the
    denominator (`r sum(genomics_only)` papers).
- **Counts with several models per paper:** predictors and terms are taken
  from the largest model in the paper, and N/k from the model with the
  smallest N/k.
- **Treatment-by-covariate interactions:** among experimental studies
  (including those with both experimental and observational parts), an
  interaction between a manipulated treatment and a variable that was
  measured rather than assigned (sex, population, species, site, date, ...).
  Two borderline cases are counted.

Percentages are followed by exact binomial 95% confidence intervals.

## Results

```{r by-journal}
coding |>
  count(journal, uses_glm_2plus) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = uses_glm_2plus, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  mutate(total = y + n, `% GLM >= 2` = round(100 * y / total)) |>
  rename(`GLM >= 2 predictors` = y, other = n) |>
  kable()
```

```{r summary}
n_bayes <- sum(coding$uses_glm_2plus == "n" & grepl("^Bayesian", coding$model_class))
many <- glm$n_explanatory_max >= 6
## N_over_k_min: Inf = "large", NA = unknown
low_nk <- many & !is.na(glm$N_over_k_min) & glm$N_over_k_min < 3
big <- glm$n_terms_max > 5
selected <- !grepl("^none", glm$model_selection) & glm$model_selection != ""
expt <- filter(glm, design != "observational")

comparison <- tribble(
  ~quantity, ~`2007 (F&S)`, ~`2026`,
  "Empirical studies using GLMs with >= 2 predictors", pct(28, 50), pct(n_glm, n_emp),
  "... counting Bayesian regressions too", "", pct(n_glm + n_bayes, n_emp),
  "Studies with 6 or more predictors", pct(6, 28), pct(sum(many), n_glm),
  "... of which N/k < 3", pct(3, 6),
    sprintf("%d/%d (N/k known for %d)", sum(low_nk), sum(many), sum(many & !is.na(glm$N_over_k_min))),
  "Interactions considered", "80%", pct(sum(glm$interactions == "y"), n_glm),
  "Experimental studies with treatment x covariate interactions", pct(6, 11),
    pct(sum(grepl("^y", expt$trt_x_covariate)), nrow(expt)),
  "Models with > 5 terms that were simplified", pct(16, 16), pct(sum(big & selected), sum(big)),
  "Any model selection or simplification", "", pct(sum(selected), n_glm),
  "Full model presented", pct(2, 28), pct(sum(grepl("^y", glm$full_model_presented)), n_glm),
  "Multiple-comparison correction across model terms", "not reported", pct(sum(!grepl("^none", glm$mcc) & glm$mcc != ""), n_glm),
  "Post hoc pairwise adjustment (Tukey, Bonferroni, ...)", "not reported", pct(sum(!grepl("^none", glm$posthoc_adjustment) & glm$posthoc_adjustment != ""), n_glm),
  "Either correction applied only after selection (minimal k)", "", pct(sum(grepl("minimal k", paste(glm$mcc, glm$posthoc_adjustment))), n_glm)
)
kable(comparison)
```

### Model selection methods (2026)

```{r selection}
glm |>
  mutate(method = case_when(
    grepl("^none", model_selection) | model_selection == "" ~ "none",
    grepl("backward|p-value|LRT", model_selection, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "p-value/LRT based",
    grepl("AIC|IC-based|dredge", model_selection) ~ "information criterion",
    TRUE ~ "other")) |>
  count(method) |>
  kable()
```

## Caveats

- F&S do not say how their 50 studies were chosen.
- For several papers the candidate models are only in the supplement; these
  are flagged `confidence = low/medium` in `coding.csv`.
- With 10 papers per journal, the per-journal percentages are rough
  (a 95% binomial CI for 5/10 is about 19–81%).
- Choosing the random-effects structure (by AIC or otherwise) is not counted
  as model selection. Whether it should be is an open question:
  @matuschekBalancingTypeError2017 recommend backward selection of random
  effects with a relaxed p-value criterion, and their simulations show
  little type I error inflation from doing so.
